_comment: Editor UI metadata for MPC SOS Fade — labels, groups, plain-English descriptions, the 'essentials' (core) flag, conditional visibility (show_if), toggle option labels, and tuning guides. Read by the command-center scanner (strategies/python/<pkg>/<pkg>.meta.json) and overlaid onto the schema built from SosFadeConfig. UI ONLY: it never touches a trade decision or the source hash, so editing it needs no re-parity — but DO click Scan Strategies after editing. Param order here is the canonical UI order. Every show_if below was verified against the code, not assumed: exec_fvg_deep_only deliberately has NO condition (it still filters which FVGs qualify when Require FVG is off), and div_rsi_len/div_pivot_len have none either (they drive the divergence that ARMS the setup, which show_div does not gate — show_div only gates the veto and the live DIV flag). LABELS AND DESCRIPTIONS ARE SHARED WITH THE PINE (2026-08-02): every `label` here is byte-identical to that input's title in indicators/mpc_strategy.pine (minus Pine's leading '   ↳ ' indent marker), and every `desc` is that input's tooltip verbatim. One parameter, one name, one explanation, two UIs. Change a label or a desc and change the Pine in the same commit, or the two panels start teaching different things. The ONE allowed deviation is a suffix stating a fact true only of THIS runner — exec_conf_sz carries '(not supported)' because the Sniper-Zone entry is Pine-only.
edge: It fades exhaustion, but only after structure agrees. Price grabs liquidity (a sweep of a known high/low) or prints a momentum divergence at an extreme; a shift of structure (SOS) confirms the tide actually turned; then it waits for a DEEP pullback into the fib zone and buys/sells the imbalance left behind on a clean fib line. Nothing is chased — every entry is a resting limit into a retracement. The default is the deep-entry combo: arm on liquidity sweeps, require the gap to sit fully past 0.5, and re-price a deep gap to the nearest fib (0.618/0.702/0.786) rather than its own edge. That combo measured about +237% at PF 6.2 / 85% win / 13% max drawdown over ~2 years of gold at 84 trades. The other lever is the HTF bias filter, which currently does nothing (both set to Ignore): this bot shorted a +75% bull market and won, so shorts carry most of the profit. That concentration is the open question.

steps.label: 01 · Arm
steps.title: Something looks exhausted
steps.detail: A liquidity sweep runs stops past a known high/low — the default arming trigger. (An RSI divergence at an overbought/oversold extreme can arm it too, but that's off by default now.)

steps.label: 02 · SOS
steps.title: Structure confirms it
steps.detail: A shift of structure breaks the other way within the staleness window. Without this the setup is just a guess and it never arms.

steps.label: 03 · Zone
steps.title: Wait for the pullback
steps.detail: Price retraces DEEP into the 0.5–0.886 fib band of the SOS leg and a live fair-value gap sitting fully past 0.5 overlaps it. A deep gap enters at the nearest fib just shallower (0.618/0.702/0.786) rather than the gap's own edge; a shallow gap enters at its edge. Always a resting limit — never a chase.

steps.label: 04 · Manage
steps.title: Ladder out
steps.detail: Take 30% at TP1 and move the stop to breakeven, 40% at TP2 and move the stop to TP1, then trail the runner. The runner is where the money is made.

params.name: exec_arm_div
params.label: Arm on RSI divergence
params.desc: Stage 1 trigger. Lets a setup arm on a confirmed RSI divergence. Both arm sources off means no trades at all. This does not control the veto — that has its own toggle.

params.name: exec_arm_sweep
params.label: Arm on liquidity sweep
params.desc: Stage 1 trigger. Lets a setup arm on a liquidity sweep — H4, previous day, or a session high/low. Turn this off and leave divergence on to test divergence-armed setups alone.

params.name: aplus_window
params.label: Max time: sweep → SOS (minutes)
params.desc: How long an armed sweep stays valid. The SOS must fire within this many minutes of it. The real kill switch is narrative — an opposite SOS disarms the setup — so this only filters very old sweeps. 4320 = 3 days.
guide: Only fresh confirmations count — fewer setups
Stale exhaustion can still trigger days later

params.name: exec_req_fvg
params.label: Require an FVG in the zone
params.desc: On = only enter when a live gap overlaps the 0.5-0.886 zone. Off = fall back to the 0.618 fib and enter on the retrace alone. Off does not switch off the gap rules below — a qualifying gap still prices the entry first.

params.name: exec_fvg_deep_only
params.label: Gap must sit fully past 0.5
params.desc: On = the whole gap must sit past 0.5, on the deep side. Off = any gap touching the 0.5-0.886 band counts. On is stricter and takes fewer setups.

params.name: exec_fvg_pre_zone
params.label: Gap must pre-date the zone
params.desc: On = a gap only counts if it was already there when price first tagged 0.5. A gap printed by the reversal candle itself is the retrace confirming itself. Off by default. Measured 2020-2026: 165 trades / +126.68R becomes 148 / +105.22R, and nearly all of that gap is one +16.5R trade — the other 17 setters it removes are worth +4R between them. Judge it on the logic, not the R.

params.name: exec_fib_overlap
params.label: Gap on a fib → enter on the fib
params.desc: Fires only when a fib level sits inside the gap body. On = rest the limit on that level — the shallowest if there are several — instead of at the gap edge, so the order sits inside the imbalance rather than in front of it. 0.886 is never used as a target: the stop sits there, and a zero stop distance cancels the order.

params.name: exec_fib_deep_edge
params.label: Floating gap → its own deep edge
params.desc: For a gap that holds no fib level and floats deeper than 0.618. On = rest at the gap's own far edge. It is the only deep rule that always fills, because the limit sits inside the gap. Measured worse than nearest-fib over 2020-2026, so it ships off. It overrides the two rules below.

params.name: exec_fib_nearest
params.label: Floating gap → nearest fib (either side)
params.desc: Same gap as the rule above. On = measure the distance to the fib above and the fib below, and rest on whichever is closer. This fixes a gap sitting just short of 0.702 being entered way back at 0.618. Not free: when the deeper level wins, the limit sits past the gap, so a setup that only tags the gap never fills. Deeper entry and a tighter stop, paid for in fill rate.

params.name: exec_deep_fib
params.label: Floating gap → nearest fib shallower
params.desc: The original one-sided version of the two rules above, kept so old results reproduce. A floating gap rests at the nearest fib shallower than it — the level price reaches first. It never looks at the level below the gap, however much closer that one is. Only reachable with both rules above off.

params.name: exec_htf_weekly
params.label: Weekly bias requirement
params.desc: A separate gate from the exhaustion filter, and it works whether that is on or off. Judges the weekly bias against the trade direction. Ignore = off. Must agree = weekly matches the trade. Must not oppose = neutral passes. Must oppose = weekly must be against the trade. Weekly must-oppose plus daily must-agree is a forming reversal.
guide: Ignore = no filter, trade every setup
Must agree = only with the weekly trend

params.name: exec_htf_daily
params.label: Daily bias requirement
params.desc: The same four choices as weekly, judged on the daily bias. Ignore = off.

params.name: exec_htf_exhaust_only
params.label: Only fade HTF exhaustion, not breakouts
params.desc: On = block a reversal that fights a fresh higher-timeframe breakout, while still allowing one that fades an exhaustion sweep. Off = no HTF filter, and the source below is greyed out.

params.name: exec_htf_source
params.label: HTF exhaustion source
params.desc: Which higher timeframe the breakout block reads. Weekly blocks the fewest trades. Either — a weekly or a daily breakout — blocks the most.

params.name: exec_risk_pct
params.label: Risk % per trade
params.desc: How much of the account each trade risks. Position size is worked back from this and the stop distance, so a tighter stop buys a bigger position at the same risk.
guide: Smaller swings, slower growth
Bigger swings — 10% is already aggressive

params.name: exec_sl_level
params.label: Stop fib level (deep side of 0.5)
params.desc: Which fib level the stop sits at, measured on the SOS leg. Default 0.886 is just past the deep edge of the entry band, and is the tested setting. 1.0 is the leg origin — widest and safest structurally, but measured 75.7R against 0.886's 109.5R. The three tighter levels can put the stop on top of the entry, which balloons position size, so turn on the minimum stop distance first. Custom takes any ratio you type.

params.name: exec_sl_custom
params.label: Custom stop fib level
params.desc: The exact retracement of the SOS leg to put the stop at, when Stop level is set to Custom. Anything above 0 and up to 1.0 — so 0.9, which the dropdown never offered, sits between the 0.886 default and the 1.0 leg origin. Typing 0.886 here is identical to picking 0.886 above, to the last decimal place, so switching to Custom changes nothing until you move the number. DEEPER (towards 1.0) is the safe direction: a wider stop, a smaller position, more room before the setup is wrong. SHALLOWER than 0.886 is the dangerous half — the entry is a resting limit inside the 0.5-0.886 band, so a stop above the fill either cancels the trade outright or leaves a stop distance so small the position size balloons. Turn Minimum stop distance on before going there. Note this level has no TradingView equivalent yet, so a run using it can't be checked against the chart.
guide: Tighter stop, bigger position, less room to be right
Wider stop, smaller position, closer to the leg origin

params.name: exec_sl_deep
params.label: Entries at 0.786 or deeper stop at 1.0
params.desc: On = an entry that fills at 0.786 or deeper puts its stop at the leg origin (1.0) instead. Why: the entry band and the stop share the 0.886 line, so a 0.786 entry has only 0.100 of the leg behind it, and a 30-cent gold spread eats a quarter of the tightest ones. It costs R on every trade it touches — a 0.786 entry goes from a 7.86R runner to 3.67R at under half the size. Off by default.

params.name: exec_sl_buf_tk
params.label: Stop buffer beyond the level (ticks)
params.desc: Extra room beyond the chosen stop level, in ticks, so a wick through it does not clip you.
guide: Stop sits exactly on the level
More room for wicks, wider risk per trade

params.name: exec_min_stop_mode
params.label: Minimum stop distance
params.desc: Skip a setup whose stop sits closer to the entry than the floor below. Percent of price scales itself as gold runs 1200 to 3300. Fixed dollars is one flat number at both ends. ATR multiple is the only one that reacts to a quiet versus a violent market at the same price. This is an entry filter and has nothing to do with the runner trail.

params.name: exec_min_stop_val
params.label: Minimum stop floor (unit = mode above)
params.desc: The unit follows the mode above: a percent, dollars of price, or an ATR multiple. Mild floors (0.10% / $1.50 / 0.5 ATR) refuse 3-6 of 188 trades and are slightly positive. Harder floors start eating winners.
guide: Almost nothing is refused
Refuses real trades, not just degenerate ones

params.name: exec_tp1_pct
params.label: TP1 size %
params.desc: How much of the position the TP1 limit banks. Default 0 = bank nothing and ride the whole position to the runner, which tested best. The TP1 price still matters at 0 — touching it is what moves the stop to breakeven.
guide: More size left for the runner
Bank more early, smaller runner

params.name: exec_tp2_pct
params.label: TP2 size %
params.desc: How much of the position the TP2 limit banks. Default 0 = bank nothing. Touching TP2 still lifts the stop to its floor and hands the runner to the trail.
guide: Bigger runner
Bank more at TP2, smaller runner

params.name: exec_be_buf_tk
params.label: Breakeven buffer (ticks)
params.desc: The breakeven stop sits this far past the entry, so a scratch still covers costs. This is why TradingView reports no breakevens — the exit books a few cents, so it files as a winner. The trade label counts them honestly.
guide: True breakeven
Locks in more, stopped out sooner

params.name: exec_runner_trail
params.label: Runner trail method
params.desc: How the runner is trailed once TP2 is hit, and which setting below is live. Fixed step is a dollar grid. Structure parks the stop at the last confirmed swing — it breathes with the trend, but a swing lags, so it hands a lot back at the turn. Structure + % ratchet is the default: the same anchor, but the stop climbs one step per step of favourable move. Measured over 6.6 years, that lifted the share of each run actually banked from 43% to 53% on the same 164 trades.
guide: Fixed step — mechanical, worst on a multi-year price range
Structure + % ratchet — keeps ~53% of each run instead of ~43%

params.name: exec_struct_trail_buf_tk
params.label: Structure trail buffer (ticks)
params.desc: Used by both structure trail methods. The runner stop sits this many ticks beyond the last confirmed swing, so a wick through the swing does not clip it.
guide: Tight to the swing — clipped by wicks
Wide of the swing — survives noise, gives back more

params.name: exec_trail_pct
params.label: Runner ratchet step (% of price)
params.desc: The stop starts at the last confirmed swing and climbs one step of this size for every step of favourable move. A percent rather than dollars because gold ran 1,500 to 3,400 — $20 is a 1.3% trail at one end and 0.6% at the other. Below about 0.5 it starts clipping runners.
guide: Below 0.5 — clips runners, costs real edge
Above 2.5 — barely binds, back to the plain structure trail

params.name: exec_trail_step
params.label: Runner trail step ($ of price)
params.desc: Read by two settings, so it is never greyed out: the fixed-step trail, and the one-trail-step-behind stop floor. On gold 1 pip is 10 cents of price, so 50 pips = 5.0.
guide: Tighter trail — banks sooner, cuts runners short
Looser trail — lets winners breathe, gives back more

params.name: exec_tp2_stop_mode
params.label: TP2 → stop floor
params.desc: What the stop floor becomes the moment TP2 is hit, before the runner trail takes over. TP1 price is tight and can scratch the runner on the first pullback. Breakeven gives it the most room. One trail step behind keeps it under the high-water mark. The trail can still tighten past this floor.
guide: TP1 price — protects the gain, scratches runners
Breakeven — maximum room for the runner

params.name: exec_close_opp_sos
params.label: Close on opposite SOS
params.desc: On = force-close the trade if an opposite SOS fires before the stop or a target, on the view that an opposite SOS is early proof the reversal failed. Off = let the stop or a target resolve every trade.

params.name: show_div
params.label: Track RSI divergence (REQUIRED — arms setups + veto)
params.desc: Detects regular divergence at the extremes: price makes a lower low while RSI makes a higher low from oversold, or the overbought mirror. Confirmation lags by the pivot width, so the signal prints a few bars after the actual extreme. Entries need this — turning it off disarms the divergence trigger and the veto.

params.name: div_rsi_len
params.label: RSI length
params.desc: The RSI lookback. 14 is standard. Shorter reacts faster and prints more divergences.
guide: Twitchier RSI, more divergences
Smoother RSI, fewer but cleaner

params.name: div_pivot_len
params.label: Pivot width (bars)
params.desc: How many bars either side of a turn confirm it as a pivot. This is also the lag — a divergence cannot print until this many bars after the extreme. Wider means fewer and cleaner signals.
guide: Confirms sooner, more noise
Confirms later, only real pivots

params.name: div_valid_bars
params.label: Divergence valid for (bars)
params.desc: How long a divergence keeps counting as live confluence on a setup.
guide: Expires fast
Stays live longer

params.name: div_veto
params.label: Veto setups on extreme/divergence
params.desc: On = block a long when bearish divergence is live or RSI is extremely overbought, and the mirror for shorts. This is where the veto is built; the execution toggle only decides whether entries obey it.

params.name: exec_respect_veto
params.label: Respect divergence/extreme veto
params.desc: On = an opposing divergence live at the SOS, or RSI at an extreme, blocks that side. The veto itself is built in the RSI divergence group — switch it off there and this has nothing to obey.

params.name: div_extreme_ob
params.label: Extreme overbought
params.desc: RSI at or above this counts as extremely overbought, which vetoes longs. Higher = fewer vetoes.
guide: Vetoes longs more often
Only vetoes at a true extreme

params.name: div_extreme_os
params.label: Extreme oversold
params.desc: RSI at or below this counts as extremely oversold, which vetoes shorts. Lower = fewer vetoes.
guide: Only vetoes at a true extreme
Vetoes shorts more often

params.name: exec_aplus
params.label: Trade A+ setups
params.desc: On = the A+ reversal setup trades normally. Off = no A+ entry ever fires. Turn it off with B-Leg on to read the B leg on its own.

params.name: exec_bleg
params.label: Trade B-Leg setups
params.desc: Adds the B leg as a second setup type. It arms when a reversal setup dies on a continuation break before it retraced, freezes the 0.382-0.5 band of that leg, and rests a limit at the 0.5 edge. Stop beyond fib 1.0. A+ has priority. Off by default.

params.name: exec_longs
params.label: Trade longs
params.desc: On = long setups may trade. Off = shorts only.

params.name: exec_shorts
params.label: Trade shorts
params.desc: On = short setups may trade. Off = longs only.

params.name: exec_secondary
params.label: Secondary re-entries (1m SOS)
params.desc: Add the 1-minute sniper re-entry: after the 15m primary reaches breakeven and price falls back into the zone, a 1m shift of structure re-enters. Needs a RECENT window (the broker serves ~35 days of 1m). Rare — ~3 fires in 2 years.

params.name: exec_conf_sz
params.label: Allow Sniper Zone as entry confirmation (not supported)
params.desc: On = the Sniper Zone (the 0.5-0.618 pocket) also counts as entry confirmation, but only on a leg with no qualifying gap. The limit rests at the far side, around 0.618. Existing trades do not change; any new one is a leg that previously logged no FVG. NOT ported to this bot — leave it off; turning it on changes nothing on a lab run, and the Pine-parity check refuses an export taken with it on.

params.name: exec_no_late_day
params.label: No entries in the final hour (16:00-17:00 NY)
params.desc: On = no new entries in the last hour before the daily close. Gold closes 17:00 New York and reopens at 18:00, so this bars 16:00-17:00 New York. It stops trades that get gapped out over the break.

params.name: flat_by_close
params.label: Flat by close
params.desc: Close everything before the daily close instead of holding overnight. Off by default, and that was measured: over 6.5 months, OFF made $39,454 (PF 1.44) and ON made $19,813 (PF 1.25). Only 4 trades ever held overnight — all winners, making 70% of the profit — against $36.80 of total swap. Flatting early buys a smaller drawdown for half the profit.

params.name: flat_by_close_min
params.label: Flatten this early
params.desc: How many minutes before the daily close to force everything flat.
guide: Hold closer to the bell
Exit earlier, more of the close avoided

params.name: exec_scratch_r
params.label: Scratch band
params.desc: Reporting only — it never changes a trade. A closed trade landing within this much of breakeven is graded SCRATCH instead of a win or a loss. It matters because this bot scratches a lot: 17 of 40 trades finished near breakeven.
guide: Fewer trades called scratch
More near-breakeven trades called scratch

params.name: fill_model
params.label: Fill model
params.desc: How fills are priced. 'bar' = the Pine's own intrabar guess with zero costs (the parity mode). 'tick' = real Vantage bid/ask fills with measured spread, slippage, and swap — what a real backtest uses. Pick 'tick' for any number you'll trust.

params.name: account_profile
params.label: Account profile
params.desc: Whose costs to charge in tick mode. 'vantage_demo' is the backtest broker (zero commission, real Vantage swap) so results match the VANTAGE_XAUUSD TradingView feed. The puprime_* profiles are the live broker's tiers, kept for reference. Ignored in bar mode.

params.name: symbol
params.label: Broker symbol
params.desc: The MT5 symbol the tick pull requests. Vantage gold is 'XAUUSD' (no '.s' suffix — that was PU Prime). Ignored in bar mode.
